Composite Decking
Deck Surface
New Composite Deck Surface

We’ll remove the existing wood deck boards down to the framing and install new low-maintenance composite decking across the full deck, finished with a double-wide picture-frame border around the outside edge for a clean, built-in look.

Remove and haul away all existing wood deck boards
Install new composite decking over the existing framing (joists at 16″ on center)
Double-wide picture-frame border around the deck perimeter
Add perimeter blocking as needed to support the border boards
Notch and trim decking cleanly around the pergola posts
Deck at a Glance
Size241″ wide (along house) × 16′ deep
Approx. area~321 sq ft
Height off grade~24″
Joist spacing16″ on center
Brand / colorTo be selected
Site Photos
Existing deck — view to yard
Existing deck — pergola corner
Important: this project reuses your existing deck framing. Once the old boards are removed, if we find rot, damage, or framing that wasn’t built correctly (joists, beams, ledger, posts, or footings), we’ll stop and show you before going any further. Any needed repairs would be priced separately and only done with your written approval on a change order.
Aluminum Railing
Railing
Black Aluminum Railing

New black aluminum railing around the open sides of the deck plus matching handrails on both staircases. Aluminum is low-maintenance, won’t rot or need paint, and pairs well with composite decking. At about 24″ off the ground the deck doesn’t require a guardrail by code, so this is a design and safety upgrade.

Remove existing wood railing
Install black aluminum railing along the three open sides of the deck (house side left open)
Install black aluminum stair railing on both staircases (4 stair rail sections total)
Solid blocking installed at every post location for a sturdy, secure mount
Estimated Railing Layout
Open deck edges~52 linear ft before stair openings
Railing run (net)~44 linear ft
Stair rail sections4
ColorBlack

Stairs & Lighting
Stairs & Lighting
Stairs, Footings & Step Lighting

Your deck has two sets of stairs. The back staircase facing the yard is sagging slightly and doesn’t appear to be on a proper footing, so we’re recommending it be torn out and rebuilt correctly. Both staircases will get new composite treads and risers to match the deck, plus low-voltage lighting so the steps are easy to see at night.

Back Staircase · Facing Yard
Full Rebuild
63″ wide, 3 steps. Remove the existing staircase and rebuild with 2 new footings and 5 new stringers, then finish with composite treads and risers. Stringer count will be confirmed against the decking manufacturer’s stair spacing requirements once a brand is selected.
Side Staircase
New Treads & Risers
33½″ wide, 2 steps. Re-tread with composite treads and risers to match the new deck.
Step Lighting
Low-Voltage LED Lights
Low-voltage lights on the stairs at both staircases, powered from the existing outdoor outlet nearby through a plug-in transformer. No electrician is needed. Wiring is run under the deck before the new boards go down.
Site Photos
Back staircase
Side staircase
The back staircase rebuild is a known item and will be priced as its own line, separate from the unforeseen-framing exclusion on the deck itself.
Deck Skirting
Skirting
Horizontal Deck Skirting

To finish off the underside of the deck, we recommend horizontal skirt boards running from the deck surface down to the ground on the open sides. It hides the framing, gives the deck a finished, built-in look, and matches the new composite.

Horizontal composite skirt boards on the three open sides, deck surface to grade
Matching skirting on the sides of both staircases
Vertical nailers installed behind the skirting for support
Small gaps left at the ground and between boards for airflow under the deck, per manufacturer requirements
Top skirt board doubles as a finished trim face over the deck framing
Let us know if you’d like an access panel built into the skirting for storage or getting under the deck.
Removal
Removal
Removal of Built-Ins

The built-in planter boxes and the two built-in bench systems will be removed as part of the tear-off, opening up the deck for the new surface, border, and railing.

Remove all existing built-in planter boxes
Remove both existing built-in bench systems (quantity 2)
Haul away all removed materials and debris

Pergola & Trellis
Pergola & Trellis
Pergola Refresh & New Trellis

You mentioned interest in dressing up the existing pergola, which covers roughly a third of the deck, and replacing the trellis your plants climb on. We recommend a black composite-style trellis, which will tie in with the new black aluminum railing.

Pergola
Refresh Options
The pergola measures about 88″ wide × 166″ deep. We’ll talk through options for updating its look along with the new deck.
Trellis
New Black Trellis
Replace the existing lattice trellis with a new black composite-style trellis for the vines to climb, matching the railing.
